cohort: 197 postpartum patients who delivered vaginally or via cesarean at ≥32 weeks' gestation and intended to use an intrauterine device
finding: Several socioeconomic indicators, particularly Medicaid insurance, were associated with loss to postpartum follow-up, while high motivation and social support were not protective.
mod_finding: Patients who delivered via cesarean or vaginally and intended to use an IUD postpartum were less likely to attend follow-up appointments if they had Medicaid versus private insurance.
